pull.title: feat(reasoning): decide the wire from MODEL capability AND HOST dialect
pull.body:
# What goes on the wire is now decided by two facts, not one

Reasoning controls used to be chosen from what the **model** supports alone. What the **host in front of it actually parses** was never asked, so a control could be sent into a field the gateway does not read, or dropped because the model had no knob while the host had a perfectly good one. This PR makes both facts required, and makes every adaptation say which field the request actually left through.

## What was wrong

**Gating read the model's knobs from a self-contradictory vote.** For `commandcode/minimax/minimax-m3-free` the cross-provider record resolved `supports_effort_control=False` from **one** row at tier 5 *and* `supported_efforts=[high, low, medium]` from **twelve** rows at tier 8 — because booleans needed 1 reporter and vocabularies needed 3. Gating believed the veto, returned `ReasoningPolicy.on()`, and logged `REASONING LEVEL DROPPED … discarding effort 'max'`.

**The encoder then re-invented a rung.** Command Code's `NamedEffortReasoning(_EFFORTS, enabled_value="max")` has no on/off field, so "thinking on" became `reasoning_effort: "max"`. Correct only because the user happened to ask for `max`; `REASONING_SONNET=low` would still have sent `max`. Thirteen other providers share that shape (groq / cerebras / sambanova / nararoute fall through to `medium`; cohere / wafer / deepinfra / ollama / ollama_cloud / fireworks to `high`; nebius to `xhigh`), and gemini, opencode and llamacpp emit **nothing at all** for the same policy while the log still claims thinking was enabled.

**Encoders fell through to their own default for an out-of-vocabulary effort.** `efforts.get(policy.effort)` missing meant `enabled_value`, so a request for `max` against a `low/medium/high` host left as groq's `medium` — a level *below* the ask, not the nearest one at or under it.

**The one per-model statement a gateway makes was parsed and thrown away.** `nous_portal` publishes `reasoning_effort` in `supported_parameters` for `tencent/hy3:free` and not for `meituan/longcat-2.0:free` — one gateway, two dialects — and `model_listing.py` read that list only to set `supports_thinking`.

**And there was no reference rung.** Tiers 5–8 went straight from the provider's own bucket to a vote across every models.dev bucket. OpenRouter spells tags `vendor/model:free` and Command Code spells them `vendor/model-free`, so `minimax/minimax-m3-free` could never match `minimax/minimax-m3:free` except by losing its tag entirely.

## The mechanism

A new `ReasoningDialect` (neutral, in `core/reasoning.py`) states which reasoning **fields** one host parses for one request: an effort field and the words it takes, an on/off field, a budget field, an OFF spelling, an adaptive channel. Every encoder and every provider that builds its own body declares one; the provider manager narrows it per model by the gateway's own `supported_parameters` where one is published (narrowing only — a gateway advertising a field the profile cannot emit is a profile gap, logged, not a runtime guess).

Gating now emits a control only when **the model has that knob and the host has a field for it**. Otherwise the nearest thing both can express goes instead, and the adaptation names the field — or says plainly that nothing is being sent.

Two subtleties worth calling out:

- **A host's on-value written into its own effort field is a default rung, not an on/off switch.** So a toggle-only model behind an effort-only gateway now sends *nothing* and lets the model's own default stand, instead of answering a request for `low` with the gateway's `max`.
- **An encoder's effort map is not a vocabulary.** Cohere sends `"high"` for all six rungs; Gemini folds `xhigh`/`max` onto `"high"`. A dialect declares the rungs the host spells under their own name, so the flattening is recorded as a clamp instead of vanishing. `providers/reasoning_vocabulary.py` — a hardcoded table of exactly those two hosts — is deleted and its facts now live in those hosts' dialects.

Supporting changes: an **OpenRouter reference rung at tiers 5–6** (one curated catalogue outranks a vote across strangers, never outranks the host's own answer) with `-free` ⇄ `:free` tag respelling; the ladder is now **11 rungs**; boolean quorum **1 → 3**; a vocabulary and an effort flag reconciled as one statement; `supported_parameters` read as capability; and an unrecognised client effort string now logs `REASONING EFFORT IGNORED` instead of being swallowed.

## What to expect now, per route

| Route | Was | Is |
|---|---|---|
| `commandcode/minimax/minimax-m3-free` | `reasoning_effort: "max"` regardless of the ask | **no reasoning key** — toggle-only model, host has no on/off field |
| `commandcode/z-ai/glm-5.3-flash` | `reasoning_effort: "max"` (right by luck) | `reasoning_effort` = your rung clamped into `low/high/max`; `medium` → `low` |
| `nvidia_nim/moonshotai/kimi-k3` | effort sent into a field NIM strips | `chat_template_kwargs.thinking: true` — the channel both sides have |
| `open_router/z-ai/glm-5.2:free` | `max` fell through to the host's default | `reasoning: {effort: "xhigh"}` — nearest rung at or below the ask |
| `nous_portal/tencent/hy3:free` | vote said toggle-only, effort discarded | `reasoning: {effort: "high"}` — the gateway's own `supported_parameters` states the knob |
| `nous_portal/meituan/longcat-2.0:free` | same vote, same discard | `reasoning: {enabled: true}` — the toggle both sides have |
| `opencode/hy3-free` | `reasoning_effort` (unchanged) | `reasoning_effort: "high"` (unchanged) |
| `opencode/mimo-v2.5-free` | nothing (accidentally right) | **nothing, on purpose** — and the log now says why |
| `chatgpt_oauth/gpt-5.6-luna` | `reasoning.effort`, OFF assumed spellable | unchanged on the wire; the dialect records `off=false` — an explicit OFF omits the block, there is no disable to send |
| `nvidia_nim/nvidia/nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b` | effort into a stripped field | `chat_template_kwargs.thinking` + a budget sized to the model, not gating's flat 1,024 |

## Live probes

Bodies built through the real gating + encoder path (keys read from `~/.fcc/.env`, never printed):

```
opencode/hy3-free effort high        body={"reasoning_effort": "high"}   status=200 reasoning_tokens=203
commandcode/z-ai/glm-5.3-flash max   body={"reasoning_effort": "max"}    status=200 reasoning_tokens=106
commandcode/minimax/minimax-m3-free  body={}                             status=200 reasoning_tokens=0
nous_portal/meituan/longcat-2.0:free body={"reasoning": {"enabled": true}} status=200 reasoning_tokens=114
```

Two could not be completed, stated rather than guessed:

- `opencode/mimo-v2.5-free` — the free tier answered `429 FreeUsageLimitError` to all ten attempts (two runs × five, 10s apart). The body the pipeline produced was `{}`, which is the assertion; the round trip is unverified.
- `nous_portal/tencent/hy3:free` — `400 "missing tags"`. A **bare** body with no reasoning field at all fails identically, so the failure is the route or the account, not the reasoning field.

`commandcode/minimax/minimax-m3-free` returning `reasoning_tokens=0` matches the earlier finding that this gateway returns no reasoning for that model whatever the body carries — not a proxy defect.

## Action required

None. Configuration and env vars are unchanged. The only visible difference outside request behaviour: the Models page tier badges now read **"of 11"** instead of "of 9", the two new rungs are labelled "OpenRouter catalogue", and each model gains a **"What this host parses (declared, not voted)"** line beside its capability table.

## Known and deliberate

- Where MCC has neither fact, gating is **byte-identical** to before — pinned by a capability × policy matrix that runs both paths and compares.
- `reasoning_request_baseline.json` did **not** move. That baseline bypasses gating entirely, and no encoder-clamp cell changed, so no re-baseline was needed and none was done.
- PR C owns the wire-side wording around `formatReasoningEmitted`; untouched here.
- Vertex now declares a dialect (its Google thinking-config encoder); Cloudflare, LM Studio and GitHub Models keep `None`, which behaves exactly as before.
- Dialects narrow but never widen. A gateway advertising a field the profile has no code for is a profile gap, logged at DEBUG.

## Residual risks

1. **A dialect that undersells its encoder suppresses a control the gateway would have honoured.** Mitigated by a sweep that encodes every policy shape against every profile and asserts the emitted fields are a subset of what the dialect claims, plus a second sweep asserting every declared rung actually changes the body — but a wrong *host* claim (as opposed to an inconsistent one) is only caught by a live probe.
2. **Tier renumbering changes the numbers shown on the Models page** and in the cross-provider log line. Nothing persists a tier number, so this is display and log text only.
3. **Boolean quorum 3 makes some capabilities unknown that used to be stated** off a single row. Unknown never adds a restriction, so the effect is more requests passing through untouched rather than fewer — but a model whose only evidence was one row now resolves as unknown.
4. **`providers/reasoning_vocabulary.py` is removed.** Mistral and Cohere now clamp through their dialects instead. Mistral's `{high}` is declared on the provider; Cohere's is derived from its encoder map. A future Cohere profile that gave its efforts distinct wire values would silently widen that vocabulary.
5. **`model_reasoning_dialect` constructs a provider on first use** for a provider the request path has not touched yet. One-off, cached by `ProviderRuntime`, and any construction failure degrades to unknown.
6. **The two probes above are unverified end to end**, for the reasons stated.

## Verification

```
uv run ruff format --check .   981 files already formatted
uv run ruff check .            All checks passed!
uv run ty check                All checks passed!   (repo-wide)
suppression grep               clean (no type: ignore / ty: ignore / from __future__)
uv run pytest -q --tb=line     15 failed, 7249 passed, 38 skipped in 112.26s (0:01:52)
```

Those 15 are the documented pre-existing failures that also fail on unmodified `main` — **8** websearch tests reading the real `~/.fcc/.env`, **6** PowerShell installer tests, and `tests/runtime/test_provider_manager.py::test_catalog_publication_tracks_warm_refresh_and_direct_cache`. No reviewer needs to chase them.

Version `6.2.0` → `6.3.0` (MINOR: new capability, no breaking change), with `uv lock` in the same commit.

commit.message:
feat(reasoning): decide the wire from MODEL capability AND HOST dialect

Reasoning gating read one fact and acted as if it had two. It asked what the
MODEL supports -- and for `commandcode/minimax/minimax-m3-free` the answer came
off a cross-provider vote that contradicted itself: `supports_effort_control`
False from one row at tier 5, and `supported_efforts=[high,low,medium]` from
twelve rows at tier 8, because booleans needed one reporter and vocabularies
needed three. Believing the veto, gating returned `ReasoningPolicy.on()` and
logged "enabling thinking". The Command Code encoder,
`NamedEffortReasoning(_EFFORTS, enabled_value="max")`, then had nowhere to put
an on/off and re-invented a rung: `reasoning_effort: "max"`. Right only because
the user had asked for max; `REASONING_SONNET=low` would have sent max too.
Thirteen other providers have that shape (groq/cerebras/sambanova/nararoute ->
`medium`, cohere/wafer/deepinfra/ollama/ollama_cloud/fireworks -> `high`,
nebius -> `xhigh`), and gemini, opencode and llamacpp emit nothing at all for
the same policy while the log still says thinking was enabled.

Meanwhile the one per-model statement any gateway actually makes was parsed and
thrown away: `nous_portal` publishes `reasoning_effort` in
`supported_parameters` for `tencent/hy3:free` and not for
`meituan/longcat-2.0:free` -- one gateway, two dialects -- and
`model_listing.py` read that list only to set `supports_thinking`. And the
resolution ladder had no reference rung: tiers 5-8 went straight from the
provider's own bucket to a vote across all 204 buckets, so `minimax-m3-free`
never matched OpenRouter's `minimax-m3:free` at all except by losing its tag.

Two facts now decide the wire, and both have to agree. `ReasoningDialect` (new,
in `core/reasoning.py`) says which reasoning FIELDS one host parses for one
request: sourced from the encoder that will build the body, narrowed per model
by the gateway's own `supported_parameters` where it publishes one. A control
is emitted only when the model has that knob and the host has a field for it;
otherwise the nearest thing both can express goes instead, and the adaptation
names the field it went through or says plainly that nothing is being sent.

Non-obvious choices:

- A host on-value written into its own effort field is a default rung, not an
  on/off channel (`toggle_field == effort_field`). So a toggle-only model on an
  effort-only host gets `provider_default()` -- nothing -- rather than the
  host's default rung standing in for a level the caller did name. That is the
  §1 contract table's "effort only (no toggle)" row and what makes both
  `minimax-m3-free` and `mimo-v2.5-free` correct without naming either.
- An encoder's effort map is not a vocabulary. Cohere sends "high" for all six
  rungs and Gemini folds xhigh/max onto "high"; a dialect declares the rungs
  the host spells under their own name, plus the highest rung of any wire value
  no such rung covers. So the clamp is recorded instead of happening silently,
  and `providers/reasoning_vocabulary.py` -- a hardcoded table of two hosts'
  vocabularies -- is deleted, its facts moved to those hosts' dialects.
- An effort against a host with only a budget field keeps the effort and defers
  the number. Writing gating's own value would freeze the flat last-resort
  table's 1,024 for `low` where the model's real share is 6,553
  (WORKING-NOTES 54 in reverse).
- The OpenRouter rung sits at 5-6, between the provider's own bucket and the
  vote: one curated catalogue describing this model outranks a modal value
  across strangers, and never outranks the host's own answer. Tag respelling
  (`-free` == `:free`) is a new helper beside `strip_model_id_tag`, not a
  widening of `normalize_candidates`, so only the caller that wants another
  catalogue by exact name gets it. The ladder is now 11 rungs.
- Boolean quorum 1 -> 3. One row is a transcription, not a vote, and it always
  agrees with itself. A vocabulary and an effort flag are also reconciled as
  one statement: a stated False takes the vocabulary with it, and a vocabulary
  that cleared quorum states the flag.
- `model_reasoning_dialect` is synchronous. `ProviderRuntime.resolve_provider`
  builds and caches without awaiting, and a lease exists to hold a generation
  across awaits, which a single in-line lookup never crosses. Unconfigured
  providers degrade to unknown rather than failing a request. Not added to
  `ProviderPort`: routing reads it through the provider manager, so no test
  double grows a member.

Unknown still never adds a restriction. With no dialect declared, gating is
byte-identical -- pinned by a capability x policy matrix that compares both
paths, and by `reasoning_request_baseline.json`, which did not move: that
baseline bypasses gating and no encoder-clamp cell changed.

Verification: `ruff format --check` + `ruff check` clean; repo-wide `ty check`
clean; suppression grep clean; `uv run pytest -q` = 15 failed, 7249 passed,
38 skipped -- exactly the documented baseline (8 websearch reading the real
~/.fcc/.env, 6 PowerShell installer,
`test_catalog_publication_tracks_warm_refresh_and_direct_cache`).

Live, with the bodies this pipeline produces (keys from ~/.fcc/.env, never
printed): `opencode/hy3-free` -> `{"reasoning_effort":"high"}` HTTP 200,
203 reasoning tokens. `commandcode/z-ai/glm-5.3-flash` at max ->
`{"reasoning_effort":"max"}` HTTP 200, 106 reasoning tokens.
`commandcode/minimax/minimax-m3-free` -> `{}` HTTP 200, reasoning_tokens=0
(this gateway returns none for that model whatever the body carries).
`nous_portal/meituan/longcat-2.0:free` -> `{"reasoning":{"enabled":true}}`
HTTP 200 with reasoning deltas, 114 reasoning tokens.
`opencode/mimo-v2.5-free` could not be completed: the free tier answered 429
FreeUsageLimitError to all ten attempts. `nous_portal/tencent/hy3:free` could
not be completed either: it answers 400 "missing tags" to a bare body as well,
so the failure is the route, not the reasoning field.

Deliberately not done: PR C's wire-side wording around `formatReasoningEmitted`
is untouched; Vertex/Cloudflare/LM Studio/GitHub Models keep `None` dialects
except Vertex, whose Google thinking-config encoder now declares one; no
`supported_parameters` widening of a dialect, only narrowing.
